authors: Alternative Therapies in Health and Medicine
sources.primary_role: The first primary human evidence for BPC-157 this index holds. It is held for what it is: two people given intravenous infusions at a private clinic, with blood work before and after, and no control. The reason it matters is not its result but its existence — the register previously implied no such study had been done.
sources.authority_notes: Peer-reviewed journal record identified through the PubMed literature screen recorded as bpc-157-pubmed-2026-09. Cited by PubMed identifier and by section of the abstract.
sources.limitations_notes: n = 2. No control group, no blinding, no randomisation, one site, and both participants had received intravenous BPC-157 before the study, which is the opposite of a safety-naive population. It reports that nothing was detected in the biomarkers measured over three days. That is not an establishment of safety and the paper should not be cited as one. Identified by the PubMed screen of 13 September 2026 and read at abstract level only. The full text has not been obtained, so nothing here rests on anything the abstract does not state. What an abstract reliably carries is design, setting and size; what it does not carry is methods detail, and no claim in this index depends on methods detail from these records.
